htna: Heterogeneous Transition Network Analysis

Source: R/htna-package.R
htna-package.Rd

htna estimates, describes, plots and tests heterogeneous transition networks of sequences of events produced by two or more types of actor, such as a learner and an AI assistant, a student and a teacher, or a clinician and a patient. Heterogeneous transition network analysis (HTNA) models such sequences as one transition network in which each node is a code belonging to one actor type and each edge is the transition from one code to the next (Lopez-Pernas, Misiejuk and Saqr, 2026). Keeping the actor partition on the network separates the dynamics within each actor from the hand-overs between actors, so the estimation, inference and visualisation tools of transition network analysis can show what the AI does after the learner asks for help, and how the learner responds.

htna builds the network from long event data, describes it by actor type, draws it with each actor type in its own colour, shape and arc of the layout, and keeps the partition on the results of every downstream analysis.

Building and describing

build_htna() estimates the network (or one network per cohort or cluster); summary.htna(), as.data.frame.htna() and as.igraph.htna() describe and convert it. prune_htna(), deprune_htna(), reprune_htna() and pruning_details_htna() remove and restore weak edges.

Plots

plot_htna() draws the network, plot_htna_diff() the difference between two networks, plot_htna_bootstrap() the bootstrap-significant edges, sequence_plot_htna() the sessions, plot_frequencies_htna() and mosaic_plot_htna() the code frequencies, plot_centralities() and plot_edge_betweenness_htna() node and edge importance.

Comparing networks

compare_htna() describes the differences between networks by actor-pair block; permutation_htna() and bayes_compare_htna() test them.

Model assessment

bootstrap_htna(), certainty_htna(), reliability_htna(), casedrop_reliability_htna(), centrality_stability_htna() and markov_order_test_htna() assess the stability of the edges and centralities and the adequacy of a first-order model.

Patterns and frequencies

extract_meta_paths() finds recurring paths at the level of codes or actor types, association_rules_htna() association rules, sequence_compare_htna() patterns that differ between cohorts, and frequencies_htna(), state_frequencies_htna() and state_distribution_htna() the frequencies of the codes.

References

Lopez-Pernas, S., Misiejuk, K., & Saqr, M. (2026). How AI-generated feedback hinders or helps learning: A heterogeneous TNA study of learning dynamics. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 42(4), e70285. doi:10.1002/jcal.70285

See also

The bundled data human_ai; the 'tna' package for transition network analysis of sequences with a single actor type.
